company_notes:
Context: mid-market e-commerce marketplace (vertical: seasonal apparel + home goods).
Primary pain: search relevance drops during promotions; high ops cost on current hybrid search stack.
Scale: expect 8M active SKUs, up to 20M seasonal catalog entries (holiday lines). Peak traffic: 8-10x baseline during sale windows (Black Friday-like).
Technical goals: embeddings-based retrieval + neural reranker for top-K reordering; avg P95 end-to-end query latency target <= 120ms (prefer <= 75ms for core browse use cases); cost per query target < $0.004 (avg) across retrieval+rerank.
Indexing: nightly full rebuild, incremental updates in near-real-time for price/stock — delta window target 5-10 minutes. Vector index: dense embeddings ~1536 dims, expected vector DB footprint ~2.5TB raw vectors.
Reranking: small transformer (distilT5-style) for top-10 rerank; fallback to lightweight lexical scoring when latency spikes or cost budget breached. Need model variant routing + automatic fallback.
Operational ask: predictable capacity (reserved) for sale windows, autoscale for mid-season bursts, transparent cost breakdown by token/embedding and per-query. Strong interest in Dedicated with burst and Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization.
Security/compliance: must meet SOC2-type reporting, enterprise SSO (SAML), audit logs, optional KMS key control. Data residency: prefer NA-only storage for vectors.
Quotes from stakeholders: "We can tolerate a little latency for long-tail queries but cannot have 500ms tail on category pages during promos." — Head of Search.
Internal constraints: existing search infra is ES + Redis for caching; migrating embedding store is new engineering lift. Team expressed need for Redwood to provide clear migration checklist and sample cost model tied to traffic curves.
Decision factors: latency SLOs, cost-per-query, ease of rollouts (A/B/canary), and fallback reliability.
POC success criteria (high level):
- Achieve P95 <= 120ms for combined retrieval+rerank on 95% of test queries at 3x baseline traffic.
- Demonstrate cost per query <= $0.004 on average for baseline traffic and <= $0.012 during 10x spikes (with reserved capacity pricing).
- Show seamless automatic fallback to lexical when capacity constrained, with documented quality degradation metrics.
